🚨 𝗕𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗔𝗟 𝗝𝗨𝗧𝗘 𝗠𝗜𝗟𝗟 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗧𝗢 𝗚𝗘𝗧 𝗣𝗨𝗖𝗖𝗔 𝗛𝗢𝗠𝗘𝗦 𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗘𝗥 𝗣𝗠𝗔𝗬-𝗨𝗥𝗕𝗔𝗡 𝟮.𝟬! 🏠

The West Bengal government has announced a pilot housing initiative for eligible 𝗘𝗪𝗦 𝗷𝘂𝘁𝗲 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝗲𝗿𝘀 in North 24 Parganas and Hooghly under the 𝗔𝗳𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗱𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗛𝗼𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝗻 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽 component of PMAY-Urban 2.0. Families earning up to ₹𝟯 𝗹𝗮𝗸𝗵 annually and without a pucca house anywhere in India will be eligible, subject to verification.

Each 𝟯𝟬–𝟰𝟱 𝘀𝗾 𝗺 unit will include at least two rooms, kitchen and toilet, with an estimated cost of ₹𝟱.𝟱 𝗹𝗮𝗸𝗵. Around 𝟴,𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝗷𝘂𝘁𝗲 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝗲𝗿𝘀 have expressed interest. Bhatpara, Titagarh and Kamarhati municipalities will identify suitable government land, while special camps will assist workers with applications in Hooghly.

#WestBengal #JuteIndustry #JuteWorkers #PMAYUrban #AffordableHousing #HousingForAll #North24Parganas #Hooghly #Kolkata #BengalDevelopment

Owning a pucca house is a dream for every individual. During his election campaign in Bengal, Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji had mentioned the plight of Jute Mill workers and promised pucca houses for them if BJP government comes in power. To turn that promise into reality, our government, under the leadership of Hon’ble @SuvenduWB ji, has taken an initiative to provide affordable housing for jute mill workers.

At an important announcement was made in a Press Conference at the Labour Department today, it was decided to facilitate affordable housing for eligible EWS-category jute mill workers on a pilot basis in North 24 Parganas and Hooghly districts under the Affordable Housing in Partnership ( #AHP ) component of PMAY-Urban 2.0.

Eligible worker families with an annual household income of up to ₹3 lakh and who do not own a pucca house anywhere in the country will be eligible to benefit from this initiative.

Each housing unit will have a carpet area of 30–45 square metres (approximately 320–485 square feet), with at least two rooms, a kitchen and a toilet. The estimated construction cost of each flat will be approximately ₹5.50 lakh. Of this, ₹1.50 lakh will be contributed by the Central Government, ₹2.79 lakh by the State Government, and ₹50,000 by the beneficiary. The remaining approximately ₹71,000 will be borne by the Labour Welfare Board of the Labour Department.

In North 24 Parganas, Bhatpara, Titagarh and Kamarhati Municipalities have been directed to identify suitable and dispute-free government land for the project. In Hooghly, special camps will be organised with the assistance of the Labour Department and the Labour Commissionerate to help workers submit their applications. Around 8,000 #jute mill #workers have already expressed interest in this initiative.

The Labour Department will coordinate with the district administration, municipalities, workers’ organisations and mill managements to facilitate the identification of eligible beneficiaries and the application process.

The primary objective of this initiative is to improve the quality of life of jute mill workers and their families by providing them with safe, secure and dignified housing.

Insurance distributors in India plan to seek regulatory clarity from the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Irdai) regarding whether commission caps proposed on September 23 will apply retrospectively to existing policies and future renewal payouts.

Key details reported:
- Applying proposed caps to existing books could compress future renewal earnings for major distributors, including PB Fintech, Turtlemint, and InsuranceDekho, alongside banks and non-banking financial companies.
- For PB Fintech, insurance commissions account for nearly 90% of operating revenue, totaling ₹6,089 crore of its ₹6,794 crore operating revenue in 2025-26, with ₹935 crore generated from policy renewals.
- Turtlemint reported renewal commission revenue of ₹225 crore in 2025-26, representing approximately 20% of its ₹1,098 crore operating revenue.
- Brokerage firm Jefferies estimates that a 10% reduction in new-business commission rates alone could result in a 10-12% decline in earnings for distributors such as PB Fintech and Turtlemint.
- Under the proposed framework, first-year individual health commissions would be 15% for distribution entities and 20% for agents, while renewal and portability commissions would be 5% and 10%, respectively.

Source: Reporting by Pranav Mukul

This positive momentum is expected to continue into FY27.

Every market recap is framing IRDAI's consultation paper as bad news for insurance distributors. I read it as the regulator finally doing something about a broken sales machine.

India's insurance penetration is 3.7% of GDP, less than half the global average of 7.3%. Yet IRDAI logged 26,600 mis-selling complaints in FY25 alone, up 14% from the year before. You do not fix low penetration by letting banks shove unsuitable policies down borrowers' throats to earn a fat commission.

The trigger for this is clear. IRDAI scrapped product-wise commission caps in 2023 for a broader expense ceiling. Insurers responded by competing aggressively for distributors, and some breached the limits. So now the regulator wants to pull the EoM ceiling down gradually over five years and simplify the whole distribution network into three categories.

Policybazaar and Turtlemint have fallen 30% since the news. I get why. Commission income is their business model, and less generosity from insurers means thinner margins.

But here is where I might be wrong. Cheaper distribution sounds great until you remember that good advice costs money. If commissions shrink too far, the pushy bank agent survives and the helpful advisor stops being viable. I am not sure IRDAI has cracked that part yet, and it worries me more than any stock price.

My bank tried to bundle insurance with a home loan once. I said no and got the loan anyway. If these rules pass, the next borrower might not need my stubbornness. Are you seeing this trend where you bank, or still getting the hard sell?

You should be ashamed. Urban Company Professionals are struggling with real problems on the ground, yet their concerns and safety issues are still not being properly addressed. And at the same time, the company is busy presenting grand promises about the future of gig workers and their financial security.
First listen to the people who are actually keeping your platform running today. What is the point of talking about pensions and a bright future when Professionals may not even be able to sustain themselves under these working conditions?
Secure the dignity, safety, earnings and future of your Professionals first, and then talk about the bright future of the gig economy.👎🏻

आज कंपनी का मुख्य business engine Indian Railways के लिए 25+ RDSO-certified safety spares का manufacturing है। इसके साथ कंपनी एक दूसरे business engine का निर्माण कर रही है, जिसके माध्यम से आगे चलकर इसी manufacturing capability को complete bogies और wagons तक विस्तार देने की योजना है।

1. Critical Safety Spares — वे components जिनके बिना train workshop से बाहर नहीं निकल सकती

कंपनी द्वारा बेचा जाने वाला प्रत्येक component RDSO certification की regulatory requirement से गुजरता है। यह certification एक महत्वपूर्ण entry barrier बनाता है, क्योंकि केवल approved vendors ही इन safety-critical railway components की supply कर सकते हैं।

RDSO Certification — मुख्य entry barrier

RDSO यानी Research Designs & Standards Organisation, Indian Railways की प्रमुख standards organisation है।

कंपनी के पास Class ‘A’ certification है, जिसे highest foundry grade के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया गया है। इसके अलावा कंपनी के पास:

ISO 9001 — Quality Management
ISO 14001 — Environmental Management
ISO 45001 — Occupational Health & Safety

जैसे certifications भी हैं।

महत्वपूर्ण बात यह है कि RDSO approval केवल एक बार मिलने वाली औपचारिकता नहीं है। नए competitors को भी इसी approval process को पूरा करना पड़ता है, जिसके कारण safety-critical railway component segment में entry आसान नहीं है।

एक ही Plant में Raw Material से Finished Component तक

उत्तराखंड में स्थित लगभग 10,000 sq. metre का manufacturing plant कई महत्वपूर्ण manufacturing processes को एक ही location पर integrate करता है।

Plant में शामिल हैं:

Arc Furnaces + Induction Furnaces
↓
Automated Moulding Line
↓
Casting
↓
CNC Machining
↓
Heat Treatment
↓
Testing & Inspection
↓
Finished Railway Component

कंपनी के अनुसार arc और induction furnaces की combined melting capacity लगभग 9,000 tonnes प्रति वर्ष है।
Heat-treatment furnaces लगभग 1,050°C तक temperature reach कर सकते हैं।
इसके अलावा plant में:
Spectrometers
+
Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMM)
+
In-house Testing Facilities
उपलब्ध हैं।
इस integrated setup का फायदा यह है कि melting से लेकर finished component और dispatch तक manufacturing process को एक ही facility में control किया जा सकता है।
इससे quality control और lead-time management पर कंपनी का direct control बढ़ता है।
Location Advantage
Plant Jagdari Railway Workshop से लगभग 73 km की दूरी पर स्थित है।
यह proximity high-grade scrap की sourcing में मदद कर सकती है।
इसके अलावा उत्तराखंड की अपेक्षाकृत कम industrial electricity tariffs manufacturing cost को control करने में मदद करती हैं।
इस तरह company को दो potential cost advantages मिलते हैं:
Nearby Raw Material
+
Lower Industrial Power Cost

Small & Complex Components — जहाँ Engineering Value ज्यादा है

कंपनी का product portfolio 25+ railway components तक फैला हुआ है।

इनका weight लगभग:

0.2 kg liners → 500 kg castings
तक बताया गया है।
Components railway के अलग-अलग systems में उपयोग होते हैं:
Braking
Suspension
Propulsion
Coupling
यह commodity casting business से अलग है।

इनमें से कई components:

Custom engineered होते हैं

Low-volume production में बनते हैं

RDSO certification की आवश्यकता रखते हैं

Tight quality requirements रखते हैं

Machining और assembly जैसे value-added processes से गुजरते हैं

इसलिए business में केवल casting ही value नहीं बनाती।

IRDAI proposed tighter expense and commission limits.

That put PB Fintech and life insurers under pressure.

At the same time, insurance demand has improved after GST removal on individual life and health policies.

Five years after famous tech apps hit the stock market, everyday investors are paying more than Rs 200 for every Re 1 of profit they generate.  

On paper, they celebrate finally turning profitable. But look at where that cash actually came from

Zomato (Eternal): Made Rs 366 crore in final profit, but earned nearly Rs 1400 crore just sitting on bank interest and treasury cash.

Policybazaar (PB Fintech): More than half its profit came from interest on idle cash, not selling insurance.

Paytm (One97): Made Rs 552 crore in profit, while over Rs 850 crore was non operating interest income.  

Their apps have millions of daily users but the actual core business is barely breaking even.

PB FINTECH TO IRDAI: THE PROPOSED LIMITS DON’T REFLECT HOW ONLINE INSURANCE REALLY WORKS

More importantly, PB Fintech says that if the proposed limits are implemented in their current form, they may not fully reflect the operational and servicing cost structure of online insurance distribution.

Why?

Policybazaar says its model involves substantial spending on consumer education, digital onboarding, pre-sale advisory and end-to-end claims assistance, particularly in Health and Term Insurance.

In other words, PB Fintech is effectively telling the regulator: online insurance distribution has a cost structure that needs to be recognised while setting commission and distribution-expense limits.

The company says it is evaluating the impact and will submit detailed feedback and representations to IRDAI.

New video: Ramkrishna Forgings — a company still carrying an unresolved FY25 audit red flag just had its promoters put up close to ₹400 Cr of their own cash, at a premium to market, not once but twice. That contradiction is the spine of this one.

Start with the business, because it's genuinely recovering: Q1 FY27 revenue +19.8% YoY, EBITDA +47% YoY, margin expanding to 17.96% for the second straight quarter, PAT nearly tripling. Three optionality legs sit almost entirely outside these numbers — the Ramkrishna-Titagarh Rail Wheel JV (a confirmed ~110,000-wheel utilisation base building toward bulk commercial supply), a new Mexico plant that's just started ramping, and an aerospace/non-ferrous forgings vertical that management says has zero order book today.

Then the governance update, which is what pulled me back into this name this week: promoters committed ₹204.75 Cr via warrants after FY25's inventory discrepancy and qualified audit opinion — that much was known. Turns out it was only half the story. A second, previously undisclosed ₹199.92 Cr warrant program to promoter Chaitanya Jalan has also fully converted, with the final tranche landing just days ago. Combined, that's ~₹404.67 Cr of promoter cash into the company at above-market pricing — roughly double what most coverage, including ours, had captured. Separately, a promoter-group entity holding 3.57% of the company got reclassified out of the promoter group entirely — worth watching, not a red flag on its own.

Here's the part I keep coming back to: capital delivery and audit resolution are two different facts. Promoters following through twice, at a premium, into a company they could have let ride just as easily, is a real signal. But whether the FY26 audit opinion actually came back clean hasn't been confirmed anywhere I can find — and that's the one thing standing between this being a straightforward recovery story and staying a "verify before you size up" one.

النموذج القوي لا يعني بالضرورة إن عندك حل Agentic فعّال.
في الـ Agentic AI، السؤال مش مين عنده أقوى Model. السؤال: مين بنى أفضل System للـ job المطلوب؟
وفي البزنس، الذكاء وحده مش المنتج.
الأداء في السياق هو المنتج.

، والـ Routing يحدد مين يستخدم إمتى. الهدف هنا مش استعراض قوة الـ Model، الهدف إن النظام ككل يحقق أفضل نتيجة ممكنة بشكل موثوق وفعال. وطبعاً أسئلة زي مكان الاستضافة، أمن البيانات، والامتثال مهمة جداً، خصوصاً في بيئات الـ Enterprise. لكن دي كلها أجزاء من الصورة.

لأن الحل الجيد ممكن يعتمد على أكثر من Model أو Capability حسب المهمة، مستوى التعقيد، متطلبات الأمان، التكلفة، وسرعة التنفيذ.مثلاً، مش كل خطوة محتاجة أقوى Model متاح. بعض المهام ممكن تتعامل معها Models أبسط، بينما الحالات الأكثر تعقيداً تروح لـ Model أقوى

في التفكير الأول، السؤال بيكون: مين أذكى؟ مين أقوى؟ مين عنده benchmark أعلى؟
لكن في التفكير الثاني، السؤال بيتغير: مين يشتغل أفضل داخل الـ workflow؟ مين يتكامل مع الأنظمة الموجودة؟ مين يعرف حدود القرار؟ مين يتعامل مع الاستثناءات؟ ومين يحقق النتيجة المطلوبة بتكلفة مناسبة؟

لأنك في النهاية مش بتشتري Model واحد، أنت بتشتري حل كامل تم تصميمه عشان يشتغل داخل بيئة عمل حقيقية.
وده هو الفرق بين التفكير في Single Model والتفكير في Compound AI System.

أحياناً بعض العملاء بيسألوا سؤال بسيط جداً: إيه الـ Model اللي بتستخدموه؟ وهل هو فعلاً بنفس قوة الـ leading models الموجودة اليوم؟ والسؤال منطقي، خصوصاً مع كل الكلام عن أقوى Model، أذكى Model، وأحدث Model.
لكن بالنسبة لي، دي مش الطريقة الصحيحة لتقييم حل Agentic AI.

एक कागज़ का पन्ना, एक सिंगल ड्राफ्ट... और दलाल स्ट्रीट से लेकर बड़े-बड़े कॉर्पोरेट टावर्स तक में मच गया है ज़बरदस्त भूचाल!"

सोचिए एक ही झटके में किसी कंपनी के शेयर 36% तक ज़मीन पर आ गिरें! बड़े-बड़े बैंक, दिग्गज इंश्योरेंस कंपनियाँ और करोड़ों की फंडिंग वाले फिनटेक जायंट्स सन्नाटे में आ जाएं... आखिर ऐसा क्या ला दिया देश के बीमा रेगुलेटर IRDAI ने?"

"क्या यह आपकी जेब के लिए खुशखबरी है? या फिर लाखों एजेंटों और बैंकों की कमाई का 'गेम ओवर'?
चलिए विस्तार से समझते है …'इन्श्योरेंस का नया नियम: राहत या आफत?'"

भारतीय बीमा विनियामक और विकास प्राधिकरण (IRDAI) ने सितंबर 2026 में बीमा वितरण, कमीशन और बिक्री के तरीकों में भारी सुधार के लिए एक ड्राफ्ट जारी किया है। इसी प्रस्ताव को लेकर देश के बीमा और वित्तीय बाजार में बड़ा बवाल और हलचल मची हुई है।

इस प्रस्ताव का सबसे सीधा असर बीमा बेचने वाले बैंकों, ऑनलाइन एग्रीगेटर प्लेटफॉर्म्स (जैसे PolicyBazaar), NBFCs और एजेंट्स की कमाई पर पड़ने की आशंका है।

शेयर बाजार में गिरावट
IRDAI का यह ड्राफ्ट सामने आते ही शेयर बाजार में इंश्योरेंस और फिनटेक कंपनियों के शेयरों में भारी गिरावट देखने को मिली…

 PolicyBazaar (PB Fintech) के शेयर एक ही दिन में रिकॉर्ड 36% तक गिर गए।
 Max Life, HDFC Life, ICICI Prudential और SBI जैसी प्रमुख बीमा कंपनियों व बैंकों के शेयरों पर भी बुरा असर पड़ा।
 
ब्रोकरेज फर्म्स और विश्लेषकों का मानना है कि यदि यह प्रस्ताव लागू होता है, तो इंश्योरेंस डिस्ट्रीब्यूटर्स और बैंकों की कमीशन से होने वाली आय घट जाएगी।

दरअसल IRDAI ने पॉलिसीधारकों के हितों की रक्षा और गलत तरीके से पॉलिसी बेचने (Mis-selling) को रोकने के लिए कई सख्त प्रस्ताव रखे हैं…

कमीशन पर दोबारा कैप (सीमा) लगाना:
 वर्ष 2023 में IRDAI ने कमीशन की सीमा हटा दी थी, जिसे अब दोबारा लागू करने का प्रस्ताव है।

 पहले वर्ष में मिलने वाले भारी-भरकम कमीशन (जो कई मामलों में 40% या उससे अधिक होता था) को घटाकर उत्पादों के हिसाब से 5% से 20-25% के दायरे में लाने का सुझाव है।

एजेंट/एजेंसी को बड़ा एकमुश्त कमीशन देने के बजाय कमीशन को पॉलिसी की पूरी अवधि (Tenure) में बांटकर देने की बात कही गई है।
￼￼
बैंकाश्योरेंस (बैंकों द्वारा बीमा बिक्री) और लोन-लिंक्ड बीमा पर सख्ती:
बैंक अक्सर ग्राहकों को लोन देते समय जबरन बीमा पॉलिसी खरीदने के लिए दबाव बनाते थे। 

IRDAI ने इस पर रोक लगाने और ग्राहक को किसी भी कंपनी से पॉलिसी चुनने की आजादी देने का प्रस्ताव दिया है।

मल्टी-ब्रांड बेचने वाले बैंकों और कॉर्पोरेट ब्रोकरों के लिए कमीशन की दरें और कम रखी गई हैं।

मोटर इंश्योरेंस (गाड़ियों के बीमा) में बदलाव:
नए वाहनों के अनिवार्य 'थर्ड-पार्टी मोटर बीमा' पर कॉर्पोरेट डिस्ट्रीब्यूटर्स को 0% कमीशन और एजेंट्स को केवल 2.5% देने का प्रस्ताव है।

डिजिटल 'डार्क पैटर्न्स' पर प्रतिबंध:
ऑनलाइन ऐप्स/वेबसाइट्स पर ग्राहकों से बुनियादी जानकारी दिखाने से पहले उनकी निजी डिटेल (फ़ोन नंबर/ईमेल) मांगने पर रोक लगाने का सुझाव है।

बीमा का मूल्य और नियम पारदर्शी रूप से बिना नंबर मांगे दिखाए जाने चाहिए।

मिस-सेलिंग की जवाबदेही (Policy Tagging):
हर बेची गई पॉलिसी को बेचने वाले एजेंट या प्रतिनिधि से डिजिटल रूप से 'टैग' किया जाएगा, ताकि मिस-सेलिंग होने पर जवाबदेही तय की जा सके।

IRDAI ने यह कदम क्यों उठाया?

आम उपभोक्ताओं के लिए यह प्रस्ताव बेहद फायदेमंद साबित हो सकता है। मिस-सेलिंग रुकेगी, पॉलिसी की दरें (प्रीमियम) सस्ती होंगी और बैंक लोन लेते समय जबरन बीमा नहीं थोप सकेंगे।
 
 नुकसान (एजेंट्स/एजेंसियों के लिए): बीमा एजेंटों, डिजिटल प्लेटफॉर्म्स और बैंकों की फीस/कमीशन से होने वाली कमाई पर सीधी चोट पहुंचेगी।

IRDAI just released a consultation paper on insurance distribution costs, and some of the numbers are wild. Broker commissions grew 2x faster than premium. NBFCs are getting 40%+ payouts. Group health commissions as high as 93%. Distributors are getting paid a lot more, customers are getting a lot less. What it means for brokers, insurers and you 👇 

IRDAI's new consultation paper on distribution costs is worth reading if you track brokers.

FY23 to FY25, premium routed through brokers grew 1.37x. Broker commission grew 2.73x.

Motor: premium +34%, commission +259%

Retail health: avg commission went from ~10% to ~30%
PoSP-led brokers (the Turtlemint type model): avg commission from low single digits to 25-38% in 2 years
Now Policybazaar.

FY26 premium ₹29,934 cr, up 42%
Broking revenue ₹6,089 cr, up 42%
PAT ₹670 cr, up 115%
So roughly 20 paise of revenue for every rupee of premium.

To be fair, PB's revenue is growing in line with premium, not at 2x like the industry. But its book is heavily health (new health +68%), which is the segment IRDAI seems most worried about. And its ₹1,126 cr renewal run-rate is exactly what the paper questions when it talks about high commissions on renewals.

Ditto sits differently. It's advice-led and doesn't depend on PoSP or dealer economics, so caps or disclosure should hurt it the least.

My read: PoSP (like Policybazaar, Turtlemint) and dealer-linked OEM brokers take the biggest hit. Direct online players, much less.

India Weekly Market Review

September 21–25, 2026

Indian equities extended their losing streak to a seventh consecutive week. The Nifty 50 fell 0.88% to 23,140.50, while the Sensex declined 0.53% to 73,895.74. The Nifty has now fallen about 5.8% across seven straight weeks, its longest such losing run since the Covid-era sell-off. 

Sector performance

SectorWeekly move

Nifty Realty+3.0%
Nifty Consumer Durables+1.1%
Nifty Pharma+1.1%
Nifty FMCG+1.0%
Nifty India Defence+0.5%
Nifty Metal+0.3%
Nifty Oil & Gas-0.8%
Nifty Auto-0.6%
Nifty Private Bank-1.5%
Nifty IT-2.4%

The rotation was notable. Realty rebounded almost 3%, while pharma, consumer durables and FMCG held up relatively well. IT was the weakest major sector, followed by private banks and energy. 

Stock movers

The sharpest midcap sell-off came in PB Fintech, which plunged 33.1% for the week after IRDAI proposed changes to insurance-distribution economics. The proposed commission and expense changes raised concerns about the future earnings model of insurance intermediaries. 

Paytm and Oracle Financial Services Software each fell about 9.5%, while L&T Finance declined 9.2% and Container Corporation fell 8.5%. 

At the other end, Patanjali Foods gained about 10.1%, Mankind Pharma 7.6%, ICICI Lombard 6.6%, Phoenix Mills 5.4% and SAIL 4.3%. The moves were largely stock-specific rather than driven by a single broad market catalyst. 

Engineers India was another standout, gaining strongly after announcing a $450 million Dangote Group contract to provide project-management and EPCM services for a 700,000-barrel-per-day refinery and petrochemical project in Kenya. 

Welspun Corp also attracted attention after its US subsidiary won a $412.5 million HFIW pipe order, its largest such order, reinforcing the company's US infrastructure exposure. 

The macro backdrop

The week's biggest macro variables were oil, US yields and foreign flows.

Brent crude initially surged above $100 as Middle East tensions intensified, but prices subsequently fell sharply as hopes of renewed US-Iran negotiations and improved oil-flow conditions emerged. Brent ended the week around $97–98. 

The bigger pressure came from global bonds. The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to around 5.19%, its highest level in years, keeping pressure on emerging-market assets and particularly rate-sensitive Indian equities. India's 10-year government bond yield also remained elevated. 

The Federal Reserve had raised rates to 3.75–4.00% the previous week, while its projections continued to leave the door open to another increase. The combination of higher US yields and a firm dollar remained a major headwind for foreign flows. 

The Bank of Japan also raised its policy rate to 1.25% on September 18, its highest level in 31 years. The move added another element to the global monetary-tightening story and reduced the attractiveness of Japan as an ultra-cheap funding source. 

The rupee, however, was relatively stable, ending at ₹95.82/$ versus ₹95.87 the previous Friday. 

Foreign investors remained the major source of selling pressure. FIIs sold ₹11,490 crore during the week, while DIIs bought ₹16,398 crore, providing a significant counterweight. 

The Mercator Take

The important development this week was not simply another fall in the Nifty. It was the continued divergence beneath the index.

Global liquidity remains tight, US yields are above 5%, foreign investors continue to withdraw capital and geopolitical uncertainty is keeping oil volatile. That combination is weighing disproportionately on IT, financials and other rate-sensitive areas.

Yet domestic liquidity is preventing a disorderly decline, while selected domestic sectors and company-specific stories are attracting buying interest.

Stock A trades at 80x earnings. I expect a 15% CAGR return over the next 10 years. What earnings growth is required if:

1.  P/E stays at 80x
2. P/E derates to 60x
3. P/E derates to 40x (or its 10-year median)

Now comes the important part:

Can the business realistically deliver that required earnings growth?

Bottom line:

India's position isn't shifting from a complete “no” to an unrestricted “yes.”

It's moving towards a conditional model: approved investment, local manufacturing and strategic safeguards.

This also connects to India's bigger industrial push.

Critical minerals supply the battery materials.

Semiconductors support vehicle electronics.

Auto PLI encourages domestic manufacturing.

The real opportunity lies in connecting these policies into one functioning supply chain.

Now consider the opportunity for Indian component makers.

More local EV manufacturing can create demand for batteries, motors, power electronics and specialised components.

Technology partnerships may help build capabilities that would otherwise take years to develop.

But incentives alone won't guarantee localisation.

But here's the important distinction.

Allowing Chinese investment doesn't automatically mean giving Chinese companies control.

India's approach remains focused on FDI approval, security checks and local manufacturing.

The objective is to access technology without creating fresh strategic vulnerabilities.

And India already has an example of this model.

JSW MG Motor India combines JSW Group with China's SAIC.

Tata AutoComp also has Chinese partnerships in EV drivetrains and automotive air-conditioning systems.

Such ventures show how Indian manufacturing and foreign technology can work together.

Think of two very different situations.

A Chinese company imports finished EVs into India.

Or it invests in an Indian factory, brings technology and builds a local supply chain.

The second creates manufacturing opportunities, but also raises questions around ownership and strategic dependence.

That's where the policy shift comes in.

On September 23, an official indicated that existing auto PLI applications involving Chinese investment may be considered if FDI approval is already in place.

India wants to manufacture more EVs locally.

But China has deep expertise in batteries, motors and power electronics.

Building a competitive EV ecosystem takes more than assembling cars.

It also requires access to the technology and components inside them.

First, why was the door closed?

Since 2020, investments from countries sharing India's land borders have required government approval.

BYD's proposed ~$1 billion EV factory was blocked, while Great Wall Motor's India plans stalled.

But India's EV ambitions created a difficult question.

India said no to Chinese carmakers. Now, the door is opening.

After years of blocking major Chinese auto investments, India may allow some Chinese-backed companies to access its Rs.25,938 crore auto PLI scheme.

What changed? And who stands to benefit? 👇

How much of an NBFC's and bank's profit rides on selling insurance?

Start with NBFCs. Insurance commission income now eats into profit before tax at levels that should worry anyone tracking these stocks.

L&T Finance is the standout at 25.6% of PBT, and analysts at Macquarie flag it as the most exposed name in the sector, followed by Piramal Enterprises and Cholamandalam Investment and Finance. Poonawalla Fincorp sits at 17.8%, Cholamandalam at 16.3%. Even HDB Financial, M&M Financial, and CreditAccess Grameen hover around 13%.

If the cap forces a 50% cut in this income, L&T Finance alone could lose roughly 13% of its PBT.

Now look at banks through a slightly different lens, bancassurance income as a share of total fee income for FY26. Bandhan Bank tops the list at 26.4%, way ahead of everyone else. HDFC Bank pulls in ₹6,927 crore from this, 16.9% of its fee income. Axis Bank is at 15.1%, IndusInd at 15.5%, Yes Bank at 14.9%. 

Private banks as a group get 12.4% of fee income from bancassurance, more than double the PSU bank average of 6%. Foreign banks land in between at 8.6%, largely driven by Standard Chartered at 13.6%.

That's why analysts specifically called out Axis Bank and HDFC Bank as more exposed among private lenders, simply because fee income and PBT lean harder on this line for them than for peers.

Then there's the second table, insurance commission as % of PBT for specific financiers. L&T Finance again leads at 0.26, more than triple Poonawalla Fincorp's 0.18. Among vehicle financiers, Cholamandalam Investment and Finance sits at 0.16 versus Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services at 0.13. Bajaj Finance and Tata Capital are both a modest 0.08, Aditya Birla Finance lowest at 0.04.

The Legend of Willy Jeep , From Toledo to the Indian Army  🚙

#IndianArmy #WillysJeep #MilitaryHistory #ADGPI 

📌The Willys MB (and the almost identical Ford GPW) was built in the United States in 1941 as a light reconnaissance vehicle: about a quarter-ton, four-wheel drive, a 60 hp “Go-Devil” engine, and a body that could be repaired with a spanner in a ditch. Allied commanders later ranked it among the tools that mattered most in the Second World War. General George C. Marshall called it “America’s greatest contribution to modern warfare.” War correspondent Ernie Pyle wrote that it went everywhere and was “as faithful as a dog, as strong as a mule and as agile as a goat.

📌Jeeps reached 🇮🇳 during the Burma  🇲🇲 and Kohima campaigns. After 1947 they stayed. Mahindra & Mahindra won a licence to assemble Willys kits and later built the high-bonnet CJ-3B, the machine most Indians still mean when they say “Willys” or “army jeep.” The Indian Army used these jeeps (and later the Nissan Jonga) into the 1980s as command cars, ambulances, and, crucially, mounts for the 106 mm recoilless rifle

📌The story that turned the jeep into legend is the Battle of Asal Uttar (8–10 September 1965), in the Khem Karan sector of Punjab — the largest tank battle in the subcontinent since the Second World War.

📌Jarpal Queen (1971). 3 Grenadiers captured a Pakistani Willys jeep at Jarpal in the Shakargarh sector. Once fitted with a recoilless gun, it still carries Urdu markings. The regiment keeps it running, has used it on guards of honour,

📌Moral of the Willy Jeep:
You don’t need to look expensive to change a battle. You just need four-wheel drive, a gun mount, and a driver who treats “impossible” as a suggestion.

Timex Group India beyond Q1 FY27 numbers

Timex Group India is not just about Timex watches. It has a portfolio across price points with Timex, Guess, Versace, Ferragamo, Nautica, Philipp Plein, Furla and newer brands like Aston Martin. It manufactures and assembles watches in India and sells through e-commerce, 5000+ multi-brand outlets, large format stores, its own retail network and luxury retail.

The scale up has been sharp. Revenue has moved from ₹422 Cr in FY24 to ₹540 Cr in FY25 and ₹801 Cr in FY26. More importantly, EBITDA margin expanded from 8.3% to 9.2% to 14.5% over the same period.

Q1 FY27 continued this trend with total income of ₹219 Cr, up 30%, EBITDA of ₹35.8 Cr, up 63%, EBITDA margin of 16.3% vs 13%, and PBT of ₹33.8 Cr, up 70%. Timex and Guess led brand growth, Aston Martin was among the fastest growing brands, while e-commerce and trade led channel growth.

The Baddi plant produced around 4 million watches last year and capacity has already been increased to 6 million. This gives Timex room to grow volumes without immediately adding another large manufacturing setup.

The opportunity is coming from multiple directions; growth of the core Timex brand, scaling Guess and other premium brands, adding newer brands, e-commerce and getting more sales through an already large distribution network.

One unusual development has been promoter holding falling from 74.93% to exactly 51% through two OFSs. The global parent has monetised a large part of its holding but continues to retain majority control. It has consequently also increased the public float substantially.

The gaps are mainly around disclosure. Timex does not conduct concalls, so it is difficult to get brand wise revenue, volume vs pricing growth, ASP trends, brand level margins or detailed forward guidance. Royalty and advertising costs also need to be watched.

The numbers to follow now are revenue growth and margins. If 25% to 30% sales growth continues with EBITDA margins sustaining around 15% to 16%, operating leverage can keep earnings growth well ahead of revenue growth.

🚨 IT STOCKS UNDER PRESSURE FOR 6TH STRAIGHT SESSION: NIFTY IT DOWN 4% IN 6 DAYS

Indian IT stocks extended their decline on September 25, with rising US bond yields, crude oil above $100 and concerns around global technology spending keeping the sector under pressure.

🔹 Nifty IT: down ~0.6% at 10:30 AM
🔹 6-session decline: over 4%
🔹 Infosys: down ~2%
🔹 TCS: down ~0.5%
🔹 OFSS: down ~5%
🔹 Nifty IT remained the weakest sectoral index

Only a handful of IT names, including HCLTech, LTM and Persistent Systems, were trading in positive territory during the morning session.

WHY ARE IT STOCKS FALLING? 👀

The biggest macro concern is the renewed rise in US interest-rate expectations.

Crude oil above $100 has intensified global inflation worries, while comments from US Federal Reserve policymakers have strengthened expectations that additional rate hikes may be required.

Higher US rates can potentially slow economic activity and discretionary technology spending, an important factor for Indian IT companies because of their significant exposure to the US market.

INFOSYS UNDER PRESSURE 📉

Infosys fell around 2% today after already losing roughly 5% over the previous five sessions.

The sector continues to face questions around:

🔹 Weak discretionary technology spending
🔹 Higher-for-longer US interest rates
🔹 AI-led pricing disruption
🔹 Pressure on traditional IT-services models
🔹 Near-term earnings growth

OFSS HAS AN ADDITIONAL PROBLEM ⚠️

Oracle Financial Services Software fell around 5%, making it one of the biggest losers in the broader market.

Its US parent Oracle fell more than 3% overnight after reports that it invoked force majeure relating to the massive Project Jupiter AI data-centre development in New Mexico because of potential power-related delays.

However, OFSS has separately clarified that it is a distinct listed entity and has no knowledge of developments concerning Oracle's New Mexico data-centre project.

KEY TAKEAWAY 📌

The current IT correction isn't being driven by a single factor.

Higher US rates + expensive crude + cautious global tech spending + AI disruption concerns are collectively putting pressure on sector sentiment.

The Nifty IT's six-session decline of more than 4% shows that investors are again reassessing growth expectations for Indian technology companies.

WHAT TO WATCH 👀

The upcoming September-quarter earnings season becomes particularly important.

Management commentary on discretionary spending, large-deal wins, AI-related revenue, pricing, margins and FY27 growth expectations could determine whether the current weakness remains primarily macro-driven or starts showing up materially in earnings.

For now, Indian IT remains caught between the long-term AI opportunity and the near-term risks of higher rates, slower global spending and disruption to traditional services.

🚨 OFSS FALLS OVER 5%: ORACLE TRIGGERS 'FORCE MAJEURE' ON MASSIVE AI DATA CENTRE PROJECT

Oracle Financial Services Software (OFSS) shares came under heavy pressure again after its US parent Oracle issued a force majeure notice linked to Project Jupiter, a massive AI data-centre campus in New Mexico.

🔹 OFSS intraday fall: over 5%
🔹 Intraday low: ₹10,332
🔹 Lowest level in over 9 weeks
🔹 Trading volumes jumped sharply
🔹 Oracle shares also fell in the US
🔹 Project Jupiter targeted to come online in 2028

WHAT HAPPENED? 👀

Oracle issued a force majeure notice to a Blue Owl unit developing Project Jupiter, citing potential delays in securing adequate power for the facility.

The notice does not mean Oracle is exiting the project.

According to reports, Oracle is seeking contractual protection that could allow it to delay certain payments if the data centre is delayed and fails to become operational on schedule.

POWER IS THE BIG ISSUE ⚡

Project Jupiter is designed to handle around 2.45 GW of capacity, making reliable energy infrastructure critical.

A natural-gas pipeline intended to support the site has reportedly been delayed by nearly six months, while other permitting issues around the project's power infrastructure remain unresolved.

The project is part of the massive AI infrastructure build-out associated with Oracle and OpenAI.

KEY TAKEAWAY 📌

The development highlights one of the biggest challenges emerging from the global AI boom:

AI demand may be enormous, but building enough data centres, power generation and grid infrastructure fast enough is becoming increasingly difficult.

However, an important distinction is necessary for OFSS investors.

OFSS has previously clarified to the exchanges that it is a separate listed entity from Oracle and said it has no knowledge of developments concerning Oracle's New Mexico data-centre project.

Therefore, the current OFSS price reaction is primarily linked to sentiment around its parent Oracle rather than a disclosed operational impact on OFSS itself.

WHAT TO WATCH 👀

Oracle has said Project Jupiter remains on schedule and that it remains fully committed to the New Mexico project. Blue Owl has also said the notice does not change the parties' financial commitments.

The key monitorables are now power availability, permits, the 2028 commissioning timeline and any changes to financing or contractual obligations.

For OFSS specifically, the crucial question is whether parent-level AI infrastructure concerns remain only a sentiment overhang or eventually have any measurable impact on the Indian listed company's fundamentals.

Update on Ramkrishna Forgings' promoter warrant infusion — turns out it's bigger than what we'd previously talked, and there's a governance item worth flagging alongside it.

We'd cited a ₹204.75 Cr promoter warrant programme (9,75,000 warrants at ₹2,100, via Riddhi Portfolio) as a confidence signal in the FY25 audit-discrepancy episode. That one's now fully converted — ₹100.80 Cr in March, ₹52.76 Cr in June, cash fully in. 

What's new: a second, separate warrant programme — 34,00,000 warrants at ₹588 (₹199.92 Cr), allotted to Chaitanya Jalan personally — has also now completed its 75% conversion tranche. Combined, promoters have actually put in ~₹404.67 Cr, not ₹204.75 Cr — roughly double the confidence signal we'd captured, and it's cash-in-hand now, not a pending commitment.

Worth flagging alongside it, not as a red flag but as a watch item: five days before this allotment, shareholders approved reclassifying MAA Chandi Financial Advisory Services — a promoter-group entity holding 3.57% of equity — from Promoter Group to Public category. A real reduction in formal promoter-group holding, happening right alongside a capital infusion increasing it elsewhere. Often this kind of reclassification is just family/trust restructuring with no change in economic control — but it's exactly the sort of promoter-structure change worth tracking rather than ignoring, especially on a name already carrying a live governance overhang from FY25.

AI is turning computing into a massive infrastructure business.

• Global data-centre investments could reach $250 billion over the next 5 years.

• India’s operational data-centre capacity is estimated to reach ~2 GW by 2028.

• Major groups like Tata, Adani, Bharti Airtel, Reliance and L&T are expanding their presence.

• New entrants are also coming in, attracted by the long-term growth in cloud, AI and digital workloads.
But the interesting part is not just the data centre itself.

• AI workloads require enormous amounts of electricity, reliable power and cooling.

• Data-centre operators are therefore increasingly looking at renewable power and long-term energy arrangements.

• High-density GPU deployments can dramatically increase power consumption per rack.

• This creates a much larger opportunity across the ecosystem -  power generation, transmission, electrical equipment, cooling systems, construction, real estate and digital infrastructure.

• In other words, the AI capex cycle could create demand far beyond semiconductor and software companies.

The next few years could therefore see a completely different infrastructure buildout in India.

• More cloud creates demand for more servers
• More AI → higher computing intensity
• Higher computing intensity → more electricity
• More electricity demand → more generation & transmission capacity
• More data centres → more cooling, electrical and construction requirements

The companies that benefit may not necessarily be the ones everyone is talking about today. The picks-and-shovels around the AI infrastructure buildout could become an equally interesting part of the story.

JSW's Proposed VW Deal Runs into a $1.4 Billion Tax Bill — Sajjan Jindal-Led Group Seeks German Firm to Cover Liability

The Sticking Point
JSW Group wants Volkswagen to cover a $1.4 billion local tax liability — a key unresolved issue in the proposed tie-up

JSW has indicated it would not proceed if it had to assume the tax burden

Treatment of the possible large tax bill among the outstanding issues that could affect the deal

Final valuation remains under discussion as financial due diligence begins

Two sides targeting a binding agreement by December

The Deal Structure
Involves JSW making an investment in closely held Skoda Auto Volkswagen India

JSW seeking a majority stake

Proposed venture would develop, build and market passenger vehicles in India and for export

Covering internal-combustion engines, battery-electric vehicles, plug-in hybrids and hybrids

Preliminary agreement reached on joint venture structure and other commercial terms

Why VW Needs This Deal
VW has spent nearly two years looking for a local partner in India to share costs and risks — after talks with Mahindra & Mahindra broke down

German automaker aims to crack India's vast, fast-growing car market

Holds only a token share through its Skoda Auto unit despite substantial investment in local manufacturing and development of dedicated models over past two decades

Part of broader turnaround strategy — counting on India to help pull it out of a prolonged slump

The Tax Issue
Stems from Indian government's allegation that VW misclassified some vehicle assembly kits imported from Germany, Czech Republic and Hungary between 2012 and 2024

Misclassification allegedly reduced the levies VW had to pay — a claim VW has denied

VW challenging the tax demand before a court in Mumbai

Resolution unlikely before end of the year

JSW executives' position: any liability arising from the case pending before Indian courts should remain with the German automaker

NUSI CONGRATULATES CAPT. B. K. TYAGI

Heartiest Congratulations to Capt. B. K. Tyagi on being elected President of the Indian National Shipowners’ Association (INSA) for 2026–27

On behalf of the National Union of Seafarers of India (NUSI) and the Indian seafaring community, I extend our warmest congratulations to Capt. B. K. Tyagi, Chairman & Managing Director, Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), on his election as President of the Indian National Shipowners’ Association (INSA) for the term 2026–27.

NUSI shares a long-standing association with the Shipping Corporation of India, built over decades of engagement on matters concerning Indian shipping and, most importantly, the men and women who serve at sea.

Capt. Tyagi’s journey from joining SCI as a Trainee Nautical Officer Cadet to becoming a Master Mariner and eventually leading SCI as its Chairman & Managing Director gives him a deep understanding of both life at sea and the responsibilities of maritime leadership. 

At a time when Indian shipping is entering an important phase of growth and transformation, strong cooperation between shipowners, seafarers, maritime unions and the Government will be essential. We look forward to continuing our constructive engagement with INSA under Capt. Tyagi’s leadership, particularly in advancing seafarer employment, training and future skills, safety, welfare, social security and decent working conditions.

When Indian shipping grows, Indian seafarers must grow with it.

NUSI wishes Capt. B. K. Tyagi every success in his new responsibility and looks forward to working together towards a stronger Indian shipping industry and a secure, skilled and respected Indian seafaring community.

Congratulations, Capt. B. K. Tyagi!

Milind Kandalgaonkar
General Secretary-cum-Treasurer
National Union of Seafarers of India (NUSI)
On behalf of NUSI and the Indian seafaring community
